item.title: SCP-173: Just a though
item.content:encoded:
Can 173 not move in the sight of dead eyes or masks? If so, then I think we can use some substitues to keep it still.
Yet I read in somewhere that 173 doesn't move when somebody looks at it, not because it can't but it wants to toy with them. So that's not a solution I guess.
Also, I wonder what it would do if the victim's neck is protected. Would it attack somewhere else rather than their neck?

item.title: SCP-2364:
item.content:encoded:
I like this, but I can't fully parse some of the sentences. For example:

SCP-2364's anomalous effect causes any living beings which have viewed it at any point to be unable to describe its shape using any similes, including naming the shape or object anything that would suggest resemblance to a known object, instead using an abstract given name to refer to it.

I don't know how to parse "naming the shape or object anything that would suggest resemblance to a known object" and I suspect there are words missing that should have appeared between "object" and "anything". Alternatively, removing the instance of the word "object" before "anything" results in a clunky but parseable sentence.

item.title: SCP-300: Re: This is very underrated.
item.content:encoded:
Are you sure you have the right SCP here?
It just shows you random postcard-style scenes of Victorian-era England.

That's not very useful to begin with, even before the final log suggests they're at least partly contrived and quite possibly dangerous. The AW connection only makes it more suspect.

item.title: SCP-5147:
item.content:encoded:
I'm really sorry, but I downvoted. The interview went on for too long and felt stiff and I don't buy the Foundation letting random anomalies help out because they want to, nor do I buy them allowing contact between multiple anomalies.

gee0765 basically covered all of my issues with it.

I really like you and think you're an incredibly swell and supportive guy, but the critic in me doesn't want to sugarcoat because of it. I'm sorry. -1.
